title: Starting the saxophone for a supermarket opening
summary: Royal explains how a school request for a saxophonist led him to claim he played it, and his father showed him the fingering and octave key.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: You know, we sort of skipped something,
We got you playing the clarinet, you started in high school, but now we're talking about you playing the saxophone (inaudible) Apex. When did you start on the saxophone?

I'll tell you, my alto saxophone playing started very, very fast and furious and it was strictly not of any choosing of mine at that particular time. I was the concert master in the high school where I was, playing the violin, and I played first clarinet in the band, the military band. So, one day a fellow from one of -- what do you call them now? Supermarkets. That's the beginning of the supermarkets -- and one of the guys was opening a new supermarket in Huntington Park and they called up the school to find out if there was any musicians over there that could work at the supermarket, to play.

So, the music -- the person that was in charge of the music center there at the school didn't know anything about that kind of stuff. They were people that just taught people harmony and how to sight-sing and things in school. So, by chance, he called me and says, "Do you know anybody that can work in one of these school openings?" I says, "Well, what do they want?" He says, "Well, they probably want somebody like a trumpet and a bass and a drum and a saxophone, to stand out on

a pavillion and to play what they call bally-hoo, to make some music, so people will come to the opening of this new market that's opening." He said, "You know anybody that plays saxophone?" So, I took a short thought and I'd been playing clarinet then for about a year. So, I said, "Yeah, I know somebody that plays saxophone." I says, "I play saxophone." And I'd never picked up a saxophone in my life and there was four, five, six of them in my house, but I could play that clarinet very well and I was an excellent violin player.

So he says, "Can you get about four guys together and go to this opening of this thing on Saturday afternoon?" I says, "Sure, I'll be right there." So, this is about the first of the week. So, I went home that day and I told my dad, I says, "I just accepted a job playing saxophone." He said, "You did?" I said, "Yeah." So, he says, "Okay, you can make it." I said, "How am I going to do that?" He says, "Well, I have a saxophone here that I'll let you use." So he gave me one of his E-flat saxophone, alto saxophones, and he told me, he says, "Now,"-- he explained to me that when you press the octave key, that made everything that played in one scale, just one octave higher, so he showed me how to finger one octave on the saxophone. Then he showed me where the octave key was, which would make me play that one octave higher.
So, I learnt the chromatic scale from C to C and

then I pressed the octave key and I could play the chromatic scale one octave higher from C to C, so I had two octaves, where I could play anything that I wanted. So, I already knew how to play clarinet and I had an embouchure. So, inside of a couple of days, I could play all the popular tunes of the day because I could play them on my clarinet. So that's how I started playing saxaphone.
